study.question: Does the near-retention and faster inference of source-coupled uniform15 reflect reduced active item capacity, changed finite-precision arithmetic/layout, or both, and can constant lifting preserve quality while reducing persistent storage and measured latency?
study.hypothesis: Observation: full16 click AUC=0.660646940486458; ID-only15=0.660282036899905; attribute-only15=0.660427677137369; both15=0.660588611043502. Their difference-of-differences is 0.000525837492685, a descriptive single-seed interaction, not statistical mechanism proof. Mixed ID15/attribute16 p50=13.7498ms exceeds full16=11.7310ms, whereas uniform15=9.6077ms, so parameter count alone does not explain latency. Hypothesis: part of quality interaction and measured cost is sensitive to arithmetic layout rather than intrinsic ID-versus-attribute importance. Three algebraically matched15-active-coordinate operators, with either15/16 table width and15/16 downstream widths, can separate sparse storage/layout effects from dense layout effects. Zero-lift15 may retain source quality with fewer stored parameters; lower measured inference cost is a falsifiable requirement, not guaranteed. No new architecture or priority claim is made.

study.proposed_difference: Add item_coordinate_mode. native retains existing15 or16 item widths; zero_lift16 uses15-wide item tables but appends a fixed zero per item field immediately after lookup for both target/history and uses16-wide scorer/readout semantics; mask16 uses full16 tables and replaces item coordinate15 with the same constant zero before the identical16-wide operators. Context/action remain16. Copy all active initial parameters from a scratch unchanged full16 model, then discard it. Count dead columns and masked coordinates in registered parameters. The new contribution sought is a discriminating capacity/layout control, not a new recommendation architecture.
predictions: full16 and native15 same-seed endpoints reproduce prior quality/initialization; disagreement fails readiness.

In exact real arithmetic native15, zero_lift15 and masked16 have the same active functional capacity and source-mapped initial operator. Host FP32 output/mapped-gradient agreement should be within declared tolerance, although frozen BF16 trajectories need not be equal.

Under the layout-sensitivity hypothesis zero_lift15 quality is closer to masked16 than native15; absolute2e-5 AUC is an exploratory material-difference screen above deterministic replay residual, not a significance or noninferiority bound. No winning sign is assumed.

Native15/zero_lift15 save the same1,516,309 embedding parameters versus full16; lifted15 adds7,680 zero-input dense parameters relative to native15. Actual counts must be measured. Constant lift may remove native latency gains; parameter reduction alone is insufficient.

An exploratory efficiency lead requires click AUC loss<=0.0002 versus full16, fewer total persistent parameters, and lower measured model p50 and p95. This previously used data-informed tolerance is not a deployment requirement or formal noninferiority margin. Report exact loss even when it passes.
falsifiers: Failed endpoint, active-parameter, mask, gradient or FP32 operator parity invalidates the implementation contrast, not the scientific capacity hypothesis.
If all three15-active layouts have stable quality and their common deficit relative to full16 persists, material downstream-layout sensitivity lacks support in the tested range.
If lifted15 and masked16 diverge, sparse table layout/optimization remains a live alternative; a specific dense-kernel explanation is unsupported.
If fewer parameters require slower p50/p95, or source-quality loss exceeds the exploratory margin, zero_lift15 does not meet the joint efficiency claim.
One-seed success or same-seed replay does not establish robust retention, universal coordinate importance, statistical significance or a mechanism across seeds.
alternative_explanations: Seed/source-coordinate-specific initialization and fixed one-pass optimization; prior suffix/interior deletions underperformed the prefix even at matched capacity.
Different BF16 contraction lengths, sparse gradient reduction order, hardware kernel selection and Dice state amplify small perturbations; no profiler evidence identifies a kernel.
Zero-input dense weights and masked embedding coordinates increase registered but not effective capacity; count them rather than claiming parameter matching.
Construction overhead, GPU load, allocator state and loader wall time can explain isolated speed differences; repeated timings and same host settings are necessary.
Earlier learned/frozen projections and native-width branches changed initialization or optimization; their null/negative outcomes are distinct from this constant source-coupled lift.

The source improves click relative to DIN while its auxiliary tasks are substantially worse; source retention does not imply balanced four-task superiority. Auxiliary labels use category/brand24h matching and official_offline visibility is not a production point-in-time claim.
